html:
On 14 June 1941 the Soviet secret police arrested and deported tens of thousands of people from Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania to Siberia. About 10,000 were taken from Estonia alone.

The Soviet Union had occupied the Baltic states in June 1940, under the secret terms of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. The deportation targeted officials, officers, police, businessmen and their families. The men were mostly sent to prison camps, where many died. Women, children and old people went to remote settlements.

The Germans invaded a week later. More deportations came after the war, the largest in March 1949. 14 June is a day of mourning in all three Baltic countries, and the memory shaped the Singing Revolution. See Estonia.
sum: On 14 June 1941 the Soviet secret police arrested and deported tens of thousands of people from Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania to Siberia. About 10,000 were taken from Estonia alone.
